notes_for_editor: Only source is the tnlandforms.us Georgia list (one page). The list also has a 'pembroke' entry (GA210) in Bryan County, so the record us-ga-pembroke should be checked: it may be the same tower or a different one. Two WebSearch calls and the Bryan County 2018 wildfire plan (gatrees.org, read with fetch_text) mention no tower here. The savannahnow.com 2006 article linked from the list's More info block ('fire towers are fading into history') returned 403 to fetch_text and WebFetch, and the Georgia Forestry Commission history page timed out; both may cover coastal Georgia towers and are worth a retry. The story is short because the list gives no build, design, fate or access. The elevation of 106 has no unit on the page, so the story does not state feet or metres as fact. The 'Ron' note is only quoted from the page credit; the story does not say who supplied these coordinates.
